Drafting a few variants — keeping the tone short and consumer-friendly. Pick one and I’ll tighten length.

Variant A (short):
Redwood processes requests to our hosted API to provide model outputs. We may share processing with trusted service partners (a current list is linked below). Data may move across borders to provide reliable service; we protect transfers with contractual and technical safeguards. We keep request metadata for a limited time to operate and monitor the service; customer content retention can be set under account controls or per the DPA.

Variant B (very plain):
When you use Redwood’s hosted API, we temporarily process your requests to generate responses. We sometimes use trusted partners to help run the service — you can see who those partners are via the subprocessor list. Your data may be sent to other countries to ensure fast, reliable responses; we use contracts and security controls to protect it. We keep data only as long as needed to run the service and support customers; specific retention is in the DPA.

Suggested bullets (short):
• Where to find full details: link to DPA & public subprocessor list.
• Transfers: we use contractual protections and standard safeguards for cross-border transfers.
• Retention: operational logs and request metadata are retained for service reliability; customers can request retention settings per the DPA.
